author: Great Lakes Wire
title: Andy Tulleners named CCFC Women's Team Coach of the Year for second time
text:
Wayne State University announced on Apr. 15 that head fencing coach Andy Tulleners has been voted as the Central Collegiate Fencing Conference (CCFC) Women’s Team Coach of the Year.
The recognition highlights Tulleners’ leadership and success with the Wayne State Warriors Women’s Fencing program, which competes in NCAA Division II within the Great Lakes Intercollegiate Athletic Conference, according to the official website. This is his second CCFC coaching award, having previously earned Men’s Team Coach of the Year in his first season with Wayne State in 2024.
Tulleners guided the women’s fencing team to a fourth-place finish at this year’s league championships. The women’s foil squad placed second overall while the epee team finished third. Four student-athletes from Wayne State earned medals during individual competition: Reka Galfalvy won women’s epee, Salma Abdrabou finished second in epee, Anabella Acurero Gonzalez tied for third in foil, and Ludovica Mancini placed fifth in foil. Abdrabou, Galfalvy, and Mancini were named to the All-CCFC First Team; Acurero Gonzalez was selected for Second Team All-CCFC. All four qualified for NCAA Championships, continuing Wayne State’s streak of national championship appearances.
Under Tulleners’ direction this season, three athletes received All-Region honors from the United States Fencing Coaches’ Association: Galfalvy (First Team), Acurero Gonzalez (Second Team), and Mancini (Honorable Mention). The team achieved a 14-12 record overall and finished 13th at National Collegiate Fencing Championships.
Wayne State Warriors Women’s Fencing operates out of Detroit as an intercollegiate athletics program at NCAA Division II level according to its official website.
“I feel very honored to be recognized by my fellow coaches in the CCFC,” said WSU fencing coach Andy Tulleners. “Our team and coaching staff worked very hard this year to achieve the results that we all believed we could prior to the season. Our women’s team really applied themselves this season from beginning to end and I am beyond proud of how they performed. This recognition is a testament to all the hard work that our women’s team put in this year on and off the strip.”
